walkthroughs.body_html:
Revelation = God revealing himself.

Special revelation: direct — visions, dreams, scripture, prophets. The Bible and Qur'an are both seen as revealed.

General revelation: indirect — through nature, beauty, and conscience. Psalm 19: 'The heavens declare the glory of God.'

A miracle breaks natural laws and points to God — e.g. Jesus walking on water, healings at Lourdes.

David Hume argued miracles are always less likely than the witnesses being mistaken.

Religious experience: the numinous (awe of the holy, Rudolf Otto), visions, prayer, and conversion — like Paul on the road to Damascus.

Prayer is communication with God — words or silence, alone or together.

Christians say the Lord's Prayer ('Our Father.'). Muslims pray Salah five times daily.

For believers, answered prayer is evidence God exists; for sceptics, unanswered prayer is a problem. Either way, prayer shapes how religious people experience the world.

mcqs.q: St Paul's experience on the road to Damascus is an example of:
options: A miracle
A conversion experience
A vision of angels
A prophecy

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: Christians believe in three different gods.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.

mcqs.q: How do Muslims believe the Quran was revealed?
options: Through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) to Muhammad over 23 years; Muslims believe it is the literal word of God, not Muhammad's own words.
Muhammad wrote the Quran based on his own teachings.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.
Jesus was half God and half human.
